text: On 3 May 1998, Kenan Mak, a student at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu, was killed in an attack.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: After 3 May 1998, on 3 May of every subsequent year, students at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu have held a meeting to mark the anniversary of the killing of Kenan Mak.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 May 2002, the two applicants were studying at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 May 2002, the two applicants attended the remembrance meeting at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 2 May 2002 (the day before the meeting), the chancellor of the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu indicated his approval of the meeting taking place in the canteen of the university.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to a report drawn up by gendarmes responsible for the security of the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu, seventy to eighty 'left wing students' wearing photographs of Kenan Mak gathered in the university's canteen on 3 May 2002.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The students then proceeded from the university's canteen to the university's garden on 3 May 2002.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the university's garden, the students were met by gendarme Captain F.Y.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Captain F.Y. told the students that their gathering was in breach of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) because they were not holding it in the designated place, namely the canteen.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Captain F.Y. asked the students to disperse.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Captain F.Y. warned the students that 'otherwise force would be used' to disperse them.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Instead of dispersing, the students displayed a banner stating 'down with fascism, Kenan Mak is immortal'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The students chanted slogans such as 'shoulder to shoulder against fascism'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The students started walking towards the chancellor's offices of the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The gendarmes present in the vicinity used force and dispersed the students.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The two applicants and seven other students were arrested by the gendarmes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: During the scuffle, Captain F.Y.'s little finger was injured by the students.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: During the scuffle, a gendarme's leg was injured by the students.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants were questioned on 3 May 2002 by gendarme officers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants stated during questioning on 3 May 2002 that they were aware that prior permission had been sought and granted for the meeting.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 May 2002, the applicants were examined by a doctor.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants did not complain about any ill-treatment during the medical examination on 3 May 2002.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The doctor did not observe any injuries on the applicants' bodies during the medical examination on 3 May 2002.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: After the medical examination, the applicants were sent to the prosecutor's office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The prosecutor's office ordered the release of the applicants on 3 May 2002.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 28 May 2002, the gendarme whose leg was injured during the incident informed the prosecutor that the name of the student who injured him was C.G.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 5 July 2002, the Bolu prosecutor filed an indictment with the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu prosecutor accused the applicants and the remaining seven students of breaching the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu prosecutor stated in his indictment that the applicants and C.G. had punched and kicked gendarme Captain F.Y.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu prosecutor stated in his indictment that the applicants and C.G. had punched and kicked a gendarme.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the course of the criminal proceedings, the applicants rejected the allegations of the use of force by them.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In the course of the criminal proceedings, the applicants accepted that they had taken part in the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Captain F.Y. was not heard directly by the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Captain F.Y. was questioned by a court in another city, pursuant to a letter rogatory sent to that court by the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 May 2003, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance convicted the applicants of having taken part in an illegal demonstration, on the basis of statements given by eyewitnesses, gendarmes, and video footage of the incident.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 May 2003, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance convicted the applicants of having used force when the gathering was being dispersed by the gendarmes, in breach of section 32 § 3 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the judgment of 6 May 2003, in addition to Captain F.Y. and the gendarme with the injured leg, four other gendarmes had also apparently been injured by the applicants and their fellow student C.G.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance sentenced the applicants to two years and six months' imprisonment on 6 May 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants appealed against the judgment of 6 May 2003 of the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their appeals, the applicants argued that there had been insufficient evidence to warrant their conviction.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their appeals, the applicants argued that they had not been given the opportunity to examine the video footage.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their appeals, the applicants referred to their constitutional right to take part in, inter alia, peaceful demonstrations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their appeals, the applicants drew the Court of Cassation's attention to the fact that similar gatherings had been organised in the past to commemorate Kenan Mak's death and that there had never been any problems caused by those gatherings.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 9 March 2006, the Court of Cassation upheld the judgment of the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance in respect of the applicants.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants asked the prosecutor at the Court of Cassation to apply to the Court of Cassation for rectification of the decision of 9 March 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their letter to the prosecutor at the Court of Cassation, the applicants pointed out that none of the injured gendarmes had accused them of inflicting their injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The prosecutor at the Court of Cassation accepted the applicants' request for rectification.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 31 July 2006, the prosecutor at the Court of Cassation applied to the Court of Cassation's president for rectification of the decision of 9 March 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that none of the injured gendarmes had named the applicants as the persons responsible for their injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor referred to Article 11 of the Convention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that university grounds could not be regarded as public places within the meaning of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that the applicants' and their fellow students' actions could not therefore be regarded to be in breach of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that the students' failure to hold their meeting in a place other than the one for which permission had been granted could only be regarded as a disciplinary issue to be dealt with by the university administration and not by courts of law.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the disturbance in the demonstration had been caused by the gendarmes' intervention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the reports drawn up by the gendarmes who had taken part in the operation had not made any mention of physical resistance by the students.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance had not examined the video footage.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor noted that the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance had not asked the injured gendarmes to identify the persons responsible for their injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his application for rectification, the prosecutor argued that the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance's decision to convict the applicants under section 32 § 3 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) had not been in accordance with applicable law and procedure.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In its decision of 10 October 2006, the Grand Chamber of the Court of Cassation's Criminal Division observed that the transcripts of one of the hearings held by the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance did not bear the signature of the court's clerk.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 10 October 2006, the Grand Chamber of the Court of Cassation's Criminal Division quashed the decision convicting the applicants.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Grand Chamber of the Court of Cassation's Criminal Division deemed it unnecessary to examine the points raised by the prosecutor in his application for rectification.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A retrial began before the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance following the quashing of the conviction.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance rendered its retrial decision on 24 October 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Having examined the video footage, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance observed that eleven and a half minutes had elapsed between the beginning of the gathering and its dispersal by the gendarmes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance noted that neither the applicants nor any of the other participants in the demonstration had used force against the gendarmes.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Nevertheless, the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance considered that the applicants and the other students had taken part in an unauthorised meeting and had thus acted in breach of section 32 §1 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance, the gathering had been unlawful because it had not been organised in the canteen but rather had taken place outside.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance sentenced the applicants to one year and three months' imprisonment on 24 October 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sentence of one year and three months' imprisonment imposed on the applicants on 24 October 2007 was suspended.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicants appealed against the retrial decision of 24 October 2007 of the Bolu Criminal Court of First Instance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The appeal proceedings against the retrial decision of 24 October 2007 are still pending before the Court of Cassation.

text: On 9 December 2002, on account of his participation in the demonstration of 3 May 2002, the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu imposed a disciplinary sanction on the first applicant Ali Akgöl.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 9 December 2002, the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu expelled the first applicant Ali Akgöl from the university for two semesters.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The university's decision to expel the first applicant Ali Akgöl was not quashed by the administrative courts until 2004.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The university's decision to expel the first applicant Ali Akgöl was enforced, and the first applicant's graduation from the university was delayed for one year.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first applicant Ali Akgöl completed his studies at the Abant İzzet Baysal University in Bolu and started working as a teacher.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 22 August 2006, the Ministry of Education dismissed the first applicant Ali Akgöl from his post as a teacher on account of his attendance at the demonstration of 3 May 2002.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first applicant Ali Akgöl was reinstated in his post as a teacher in July 2007, following the quashing of his conviction by the Court of Cassation on 10 October 2006.

text: At the material time, section 10 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) required that, in order for a meeting to take place, the governor's office or authorities of the district in which the demonstration is planned must be informed, during opening hours and at least seventy-two hours prior to the meeting, by a notice containing the signature of all the members of the organising board.

Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibits demonstrations and processions on public streets, in parks, places of worship and buildings in which public services are based.

Section 22 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) requires that demonstrations organised in public squares must comply with security instructions and not disrupt individuals' movement or public transport.

Section 24 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that demonstrations and processions which do not comply with the provisions of that law will be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators have been warned.

Section 32 § 1 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that unarmed persons taking part in an unlawful meeting or procession who, instead of dispersing of their own motion after having been warned or ordered to do so and who thus have to be forcefully dispersed by government forces, are liable to be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of between one and three years.

Section 32 § 2 of the Meetings and Demonstration Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that, unless their action breaches another criminal law provision which stipulates a more severe punishment, persons who resort to violence or making threats while being dispersed, or who resist the attempts to disperse them, are liable to be sentenced to a term of imprisonment of between three and five years.
